stem: Which clinical feature most strongly suggests asthma rather than simple viral-induced wheeze in a child?

options.text: Wheeze only during upper respiratory tract infections
Interval symptoms such as night coughing or exercise-induced wheeze
Marked improvement after a single course of oral antibiotics
Wheeze only after exposure to cold weather

explanation: Interval symptoms such as night coughing or exercise-induced wheeze suggest asthma. These symptoms occur outside acute viral infections and reflect chronic airway hyper-responsiveness.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because wheeze confined to viral infections is more typical of viral-induced wheeze.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because many children with viral-induced wheeze improve with age; this does not specifically indicate asthma.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because symptoms occurring between infections, especially at night or with exercise, are characteristic of asthma.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because improvement with antibiotics suggests an infective airway process rather than asthma.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because cold weather can trigger symptoms but does not by itself distinguish asthma from other wheezing conditions.

source.hint: Think about whether the symptoms are isolated to illness or occur during daily activities.
